text.p: The Malaysian ringgit remained under pressure on Monday though most Southeast Asian currencies received a slight reprieve from the dollar's weakness against major currencies like the mark and yen.
Dealers said the ringgit remained under pressure against the dollar following Prime Minister's Mahathir Mohamad's comment on Friday that he was happy with the level of the ringgit.
They said the remark was taken to mean that the central bank would allow the ringgit to find its own level and not intervene to stop the ringgit from being sold.
The ringgit saw a mild repreive on early Monday morning but soon resumed its downtrend and touch a 42-month low of 2.7080 against the dollar.
"A nice objective for the dollar/ringgit would be 2.80, especially if the dollar shows more weakness against the majors," a foreign currency dealer in Singapore said.
He said 2.80, the high in 1993, would be a major psychological level, especially if the dollar/mark broke 1.90.
"Buying interest in dollar/Malay among offshore parties is still very strong, especially U.S. funds and Hongkong parties.

"I think off-shore parties are still short ringgit and long U.S. dollar, but it is the reverse onshore. Local commercials have not fully heged their dollar positions," said a dealer at a European bank in Singapore.
The Singapore dollar firmed slightly against the U.S. dollar on profit taking in dollars early Monday morning.

Dealers said the medium term objective of 1.4800 for dollar/Sing was still intact, but the Singapore currency got a boost from an upbeat economic forecast by Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong in his National Day speech on Friday night.
Goh said the economy was on track for stronger growth in the second half of the year after chalking up a 5.9 percent rise in gross domestic growth for the first half.
Dealers however said the dollar/Sing should find good buying interest at 1.4730 on the downside.
The Thai baht weakened against the dollar in early quiet trade on some commercial demand for the dollar, dealers said.
"There was some dollar bidding this morning but the volume was verly thin," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The baht eased to 31.30/31.60 to the dollar early in the domestic market from 31.25/31.35 late on Friday.
Dealers said the market was awaiting the outcome of Thailand's talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in Tokyo on Monday.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and potential foreign creditors gathered in Tokyo to hammer out an aid package of up to $15 billion to help shore up Thailand's ailing economy.
The Indonesian rupiah was softer against the dollar due to a spillover from the weaker Malaysian ringgit, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said fresh ringgit selling in a market in response to Mahathir's comments pushed the rupiah lower. However, profit-taking limited the downside.
A dealer said dollar profit-takers and selling from state banks capped the upside at the 2,610 level.

Another local bank dealer said corporate orders and foreign dollar selling helped the rupiah recover to 2,601.0/03.0 at 0240 GMT from an opening of 2,608.0/13.0. But the rupiah was lower than Friday's close of 2,598.0.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), and Doreen Siow in Singapore (65-8703090)
